subject: Deployment mode selection - hosted vs dedicated vs private (post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@novahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@novahealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Great meeting today — next steps on deployment mode selection

Sam / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for Nova Health as you migrate off your current provider/cluster.

Summary of your needs (as I understood them):
- Primary: low-latency, high-throughput inference for real-time patient-facing workflows (peak concurrent QPS ~120).
- Data residency & compliance: PHI-sensitive data for some workflows; SOC2 + contractual audit evidence required.
- Migration constraints: currently on a mix of OpenAI API for some endpoints and an internal legacy GPU cluster for heavy batch workloads. Goal is to consolidate and reduce operational overhead while keeping predictable cost.

Recommended paths (short):
1) Hosted API (Redwood) — fastest to POC (hours), good for non-PHI or masked data.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools we manage for you; predictable throughput and cost, allows mixed public/private traffic patterns.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — customer-managed networking and keys; best for full PHI workloads and strict procurement/compliance requirements.

Questions / asks for you to help us qualify:
- Which workflows must remain PHI in a private network vs which can be routed to Hosted/Dedicated? (ballpark % or list of endpoints)
- Expected steady-state QPS and peak QPS per workflow (you gave 120 peak; any burst patterns?)
- Timeline for migration (POC -> staging -> prod) and procurement windows (any procurement freeze dates?)
- Any blockers in procurement/legal for vendor-hosted vs private deployments?

Next steps I propose:
- You send back the short answers above by end of week.
- I’ll schedule a technical deep dive with Vivek (our SE) to validate throughput/quant sizing and propose Dedicated capacity sizing.
- If PHI-critical, we’ll share our Private/VPC checklist and an infra diagram for your infra team.

I’ve looped in Neha on procurement cadence and Vivek on the technical side. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min follow-up tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Great meeting today — next steps on deployment mode selection

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PHI split: Approx 60% of requests for the clinical assistant endpoints are PHI (patient identifiers / notes). Non-clinical QA/chatbot is non-PHI and can land on hosted.
- Traffic: steady-state ~50 QPS across non-PHI; clinical endpoints have bursts to 150 QPS during morning rounds (30min windows).
- Timeline: want a POC in 4 weeks, staging in 8, prod in 12–16 weeks. Procurement: procurement team needs vendor paperwork (SOC2, DPA, security questionnaire) and a commercial SOW for Dedicated pricing.
- Blockers: main blocker is procurement/legal for vendor-hosted PHI; if we can show Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS, procurement may greenlight.

Can we get an estimate for Dedicated sizing/cost and the SOC2 artifacts? Also please include any migration runbook for moving from our legacy GPU cluster — we expect to keep batch jobs on our cluster for long-tail offline tasks but want realtime on your infra.

—Sam
Sam Wu
Head of ML Platforms | Nova Health
sam.wu@novahealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@novahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Great meeting today — next steps on deployment mode selection

Appreciate the details, Sam — that’s very helpful. Summary of the plan we’ll execute: 

1) POC (4 weeks): spin up a Dedicated pool sized for your expected peak (we’ll propose sizing below) but route non-PHI to Hosted where appropriate to reduce cost. This avoids procurement blocking for non-PHI traffic while we work towards procurement approval for PHI on Dedicated/Private.
2) Technical deep dive: Vivek to run an infra-sizing session (I’ll send a calendar invite).
3) Docs & artifacts: I’ll push SOC2 + SOW + Dedicated SLA and the Private VPC checklist.
4) Migration runbook: we’ll provide a migration playbook for moving realtime endpoints (low-lift) and co-existence guidance for batch jobs on your legacy cluster + network/ingress best practices.

Preliminary Dedicated sizing (very rough):
- Baseline: 4 x NVIDIA H100-equivalent nodes for steady 50 QPS with headroom.
- Burst handling: enable autoscale with burst capacity to handle the 150 QPS morning window. We’ll propose a policy to cap spend during long tails.

Action items for Nova Health:
- Confirm PHI/non-PHI split is correct (60/40).
- Share any procurement blackout dates.
- Approve a 1-hour technical deep dive this week with Vivek.

I’ll attach the Dedicated SLA and Private VPC checklist in the next message (Vivek will send the full packet from our security team).

Thanks — Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@novahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Redwood tech packet + infra diagram (Dedicated sizing & migration notes)

Hi Sam — quick tech follow-up and attached artifacts for procurement and your infra team. Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-checklist.docx, infra-diagram.png.

Key technical notes: 
- Dedicated sizing: based on 120 peak QPS with 150 QPS morning bursts, we recommend starting with 4 H100-equivalent nodes with autoscale + 2-node burst pool. This gives sustained throughput and headroom for model warm-up.
- Model hosting: we recommend hosting the low-latency clinical model as a quantized 8-bit variant for Dedicated to optimize cost without measurable accuracy loss; we can evaluate with a quick eval on a representational prompt set.
- Migration runbook highlights:
  * Step 1: POC on non-PHI endpoints (Hosted) to validate latency & correctness.
  * Step 2: Provision Dedicated pool; run canary traffic (10% of clinical requests) with mirrored logs to verify parity.
  * Step 3: Gradual cutover of clinical endpoints when procurement approves; use traffic shaping to control spend.
  * Step 4: Keep batch jobs on legacy cluster; we provide an adapter for batching that can TTL cached KV prefixes so repeated requests hit cache on Redwood side.
- Networking/KMS: For Private/Dedicated with PHI, we support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS/HSM. Our checklist (attached) lists required firewall rules, subnets, and accepted cipher suites.

If you’re ready, I’ve tentatively created a 60-min slot tomorrow at 11am PT for the technical deep dive. Please confirm and I’ll send the invite.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
